**Meari** is the cloud platform behind many brands of Wi-Fi cameras and doorbells, often battery powered. If your camera is controlled with one of these apps, this integration is for you:

| App                   | Common brands                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| ieGeek Cam            | ieGeek                         |
| CloudEdge             | cameras sold under many brands |
| CloudPlus / CloudHome | same                           |
| ANRAN                 | ANRAN                          |
| Arenti                | Arenti                         |
| BoifunCam             | Boifun                         |

These cameras expose neither RTSP nor ONVIF: the integration goes through the Meari cloud, like the app does.

## What you get

For each camera:

- **Motion**: on for the chosen duration after the last alert (motion, PIR or person).
- **Doorbell** (doorbells only): goes to 1 for a few seconds on every press.
- **Battery** and **charging**, read from the cloud without waking the camera up.
- **Image**: the picture of the last alert, shown in the camera widget.
- **Settings** when the camera exposes them: motion detection, person detection, PIR sensor, status LED.

Two scene triggers: **Doorbell pressed** and **Motion detected** (filterable by person or other motion).

## Dashboard widgets

- **Meari camera**: the last picture, the battery and the motion. A battery doorbell sleeps between events, so the picture is updated at every alert or press (the widget refreshes at once), without ever waking the camera. The "Check for a new picture" button looks in the cloud for a newer one.
- **Doorbell presses**: the last 5 presses, with the day and time, and the picture taken at the press when the cloud provides one. The history is kept by the integration and rebuilt from the cloud (last 7 days) at startup.

In the **Meari camera** widget, pick a camera — doorbells are excluded, they have their own widget. In **Doorbell presses**, pick a doorbell (default: all); tap a press to open its picture enlarged.

## Setup

1. **Create a second account in your app** (ieGeek Cam, CloudEdge…) and share your cameras with it. The cloud allows a single live session per account: with the phone's account, alerts still arrive, but by polling (within 15 seconds) instead of instantly.
2. In Gladys, open the integration and fill in the e-mail, the password, the app used (the one the account was created with), the country code and the dial code.
3. Click **Test the connection**: your cameras are listed.
4. **Discovery** tab: add your cameras.

## Known limits

- No live video: the image is the one of the last alert.
- The delay between a press and the scene depends on the cloud (usually one to a few seconds with push).
- If your doorbell is not recognized as one, enable "Add a doorbell feature to every camera".

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Meari or the app vendors.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Meari asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your camera app account | `section` | No | Meari is the cloud behind ieGeek Cam, CloudEdge, CloudPlus/CloudHome, ANRAN, Arenti and BoifunCam. Use a SECOND account of your app, with your cameras shared to it: the cloud allows one live session per account, so the phone's account delays alerts (15 s instead of instant). |
| E-mail | `string` | Yes |  |
| Password | `secret` | Yes |  |
| Your camera app | `select` | Yes |  |
| Country code | `string` | No | Two letters, as chosen in the app (FR, BE, CH...). |
| Phone dial code | `string` | No | Without the +, e.g. 33 for France. |
| Instant alerts (push) | `boolean` | No | Listen to the cloud push channel. Off: alerts arrive by polling, within 15 s. |
| Motion duration (s) | `number` | No | How long the motion sensor stays on after the last alert. |
| Battery refresh (s) | `number` | No | Battery and settings are read from the cloud, the camera is never woken up. |
| Add a doorbell feature to every camera | `boolean` | No | Only if your doorbell is not detected as one. |
| Language of device names | `select` | No | Language of the created feature names (Motion, Battery, Status LED...). Applied when a camera is added; rename a feature anytime in Gladys. |

## How to install Meari in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Meari appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/vincentbesseau/gladys-integration-meari:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/vincentBesseau/gladys-integration-meari](https://github.com/vincentBesseau/gladys-integration-meari).

Meari requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Meari is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [vincentBesseau](https://github.com/vincentBesseau), not by the Gladys core team.
